title: Adaptive Cognitive Step-Size Control: chartStability vs. Direct sceneGeometry Horizon Jumps vs. Fixed Polling
hypothesis: Using chartStability filtered to physical sect flips provides accurate, low-overhead adaptive step-size control around circadian regime cliffs (sunrise, sunset, civil dawn, civil dusk) that beats both fixed-interval polling and direct analytic sceneGeometry.diurnal.minutesToNext jump scheduling.
null_baseline: Arm1-Fixed-Poll-30m (constant 30-min polling), Arm2-Stability-AllFlips (unfiltered chartStability reacting to angle/sign/house/aspect flips), and Arm4-Analytic-RiseSet-Jump (direct next-boundary sleep via sceneGeometry.diurnal.minutesToNext without finite-difference chart sweeps).
success_bar: Arm3-Stability-Physical-SectOnly detects >= 95% of all 4 physical twilight/horizon cliffs within +/-5 min, reduces wakeups by >= 40% vs Arm1-Fixed-Poll-30m with 0 phantom sign-ingress alarms, AND stays within 2x of Arm4-Analytic-RiseSet-Jump total CPU cost.
kill_criterion: If Arm4-Analytic-RiseSet-Jump (sceneGeometry.diurnal.minutesToNext) strictly dominates Arm3-Stability-Physical-SectOnly with >= 5x lower CPU cost AND higher physical cliff coverage (catching civil dawn/dusk that binary sect misses) at equal or fewer wakeups, kill chartStability as an adaptive step-size controller and archive to lab/graveyard/KILL-005-chart-stability-step-control.md.
